context: A long day in the rain has given you a cold. Today: explaining symptoms at a drugstore and understanding the dosage.

phrases.jp: {風邪薬|かぜぐすり}はありますか。

phrases.note: Body part + が{痛|いた}いです works for anything: {頭|あたま} head, お{腹|なか} stomach, {歯|は} tooth.

phrases.jp: {一日|いちにち}{何回|なんかい}{飲|の}めばいいですか。
phrases.en: How many times a day should I take it?
phrases.note: Medicine is "drunk" ({飲|の}む) in Japanese, even pills.

phrases.jp: なんか{頭|あたま}{痛|いた}い…

dialogue_setting: At the medicine counter of a drugstore.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: すみません、{風邪薬|かぜぐすり}はありますか。
dialogue.en: Excuse me, do you have cold medicine?

dialogue.speaker: Pharmacist
dialogue.jp: どんな{症状|しょうじょう}ですか。

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: のどが{痛|いた}くて、{少|すこ}し{熱|ねつ}があります。
dialogue.en: My throat hurts and I have a slight fever.

dialogue.speaker: Pharmacist
dialogue.jp: それなら、こちらがいいですね。{一日|いちにち}3{回|かい}、{食後|しょくご}に{飲|の}んでください。
dialogue.en: Then this one is good. Take it 3 times a day, after meals.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: わかりました。ありがとうございます。

kanji.where: In big letters on drugstore signs, often red or yellow. Drugstores also sell snacks, drinks and cosmetics, usually cheaper than the konbini.
kanji.related: Related: {処方箋|しょほうせん} prescription, {薬局|やっきょく} pharmacy.

tip.title: お大事に and masks
tip.body: When you're sick, people say お{大事|だいじ}に (take care). Just answer ありがとうございます. With a cold, wearing a mask on trains and in shops is seen as considerate. For prescription medicine, look for {調剤|ちょうざい} on the sign.

challenge.prompt: Tell the pharmacist: "My stomach hurts. Do you have any medicine for it?"
challenge.hint: stomach = お{腹|なか}, medicine = {薬|くすり}
challenge.model_answer: お{腹|なか}が{痛|いた}いんですが、{薬|くすり}はありますか。
